newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Queensland's Goss says to stand for federal seat.
newsitem.headline: Queensland's Goss says to stand for federal seat.

text.p: The former premier of Queensland, Wayne Goss, said on Wednesday he would be standing as an Australian Labor Party candidate at the next federal elections.
"I intend to nominate as a candidate at the next federal elections," Goss said in a statement released ahead of a news conference in Brisbane.
"I advised the leader of the Federal parliamentary Labor Party, Kim Beazley, yesterday of my intention and he welcomed my decision."

Goss said he did not know in which electorate he would be standing, referring to Queensland federal seats which were currently the subject of an electoral redistribution and to the addition of a new federal seat.
"It would be inappropriate to try to identify a seat at this stage, because we do not know where the new seat will be or the new boundaries of existing seats," he said in a statement.
As Queensland premier from 1989 to 1996, Goss was one of the most popular politicians in Australia.

But his government was forced from office in February 1996 after losing its working majority and Goss later resigned as state Labor leader. The federal Labor Party was forced from office in national elections the following month with an overwhelming victory by the Liberal/National coalition led by Prime Minister John Howard.
Goss, 46, told the news conference that speculation he was interested in becoming leader of the federal Labor Party was "fanciful".
But he added: "I'd like to be on Kim Beazley's front bench. The federal Labor Party is still shaping its economic policy and I'd like to be part of that."
He also quashed talk that he might stand in the Oxley seat of race row politician Pauline Hanson, saying that the candidate should be a local person.
"Pauline Hanson is not the problem in Australia. It's John Howard's fault for not moving early enough to put her in her place," Goss said.
The next federal election is due in 1999.
